study_info.journal: The New England Journal of Medicine
study_info.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; randomization was performed using a permuted-block algorithm stratified according to clinical center and age.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Postmenopausal women, 50 to 79 years of age, already enrolled in a Women’s Health Initiative (WHI) clinical trial, with no evidence of a medical condition associated with a predicted survival of less than three years and no safety, adherence, or retention risks.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Exclusion criteria included hypercalcemia, renal calculi, corticosteroid use, and calcitriol use.
study_info.study_setting: Multi-center clinical trial at 40 clinical centers in the United States.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Participants enrolled in the WHI Dietary Modification trial, WHI Hormone Therapy trials, or both were invited to join the calcium with vitamin D trial at their first or second annual follow-up visit.
study_info.dropout_reasons: Death, withdrawal, or loss to follow-up; intolerable gastrointestinal symptoms, development of renal calculi or hypercalcemia, or requirement for renal dialysis.

minimal_units.intervention_details: 1000 mg of elemental calcium as calcium carbonate with 400 IU of vitamin D3 daily, provided as two tablets per day (each containing 500 mg calcium and 200 IU vitamin D3), chewable or swallowable, taken in divided doses with meals.
minimal_units.intervention_frequency: 2 tablets per day, in divided doses with meals
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: The rate of adherence (defined as use of 80 percent or more of the assigned study medication) ranged from 60 to 63 percent during the first three years of follow-up, with an additional 13 to 21 percent of the participants taking at least half of their study pills. At the end of the trial, 76 percent were still taking the study medication, and 59 percent were taking 80 percent or more of it.

outcomes.comparison_targets: Calcium plus Vitamin D supplementation vs Placebo

minimal_units.control_details: Placebo tablets, provided by GlaxoSmithKline, matching the active supplement in appearance and schedule.
minimal_units.adherence_to_control: The rate of adherence (defined as use of 80 percent or more of the assigned study medication) ranged from 60 to 63 percent during the first three years of follow-up, with an additional 13 to 21 percent of the participants taking at least half of their study pills. At the end of the trial, 76 percent were still taking the study medication, and 59 percent were taking 80 percent or more of it.

outcomes.comparison_targets: calcium plus vitamin D vs placebo
